ACTION: ADD 
TITLE:  KernelSHAP Analysis for High-Dimensional Data Sets
PROPOSAL: We analyze the sample complexity of KernelSHAP and its relation to the number of features in the input data. We will use a dataset like MNIST, ImageNet, or a real-world dataset with high-dimensional features.
CONTROLS: Baseline comparison with the widely used SHAP library's implementation of KernelSHAP, ablation studies of the effect of the number of samples and the choice of kernel.
COST: 10,000
PREDICTION: We expect to find that the sample complexity of KernelSHAP grows exponentially with the number of features in the input data, leading to significant computational costs for high-dimensional data sets. This may indicate that KernelSHAP is not suitable for large-scale applications and that new estimators with better sample complexity are needed.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Improving Estimators for Shapley Values
PROPOSAL: We explore the idea of pairing KernelSHAP with importance-weighted estimators to improve its sample efficiency and accuracy. We will apply the technique of importance sampling to correct for the bias introduced by the random subsampling in KernelSHAP.
CONTROLS: Comparison with KernelSHAP, unbiased KernelSHAP, and LeverageSHAP on several real-world datasets such as COMPAS, German Credit, and others with high-dimensional feature spaces.
COST: 30,000
PREDICTION: We anticipate that the importance-weighted KernelSHAP will outperform the original KernelSHAP, unbiased KernelSHAP, and LeverageSHAP on tasks involving high-dimensional feature spaces, and show a notable reduction in the variance of the Shapley value estimates.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Asymptotic Analysis of LeverageSHAP
PROPOSAL: We provide an asymptotic analysis of LeverageSHAP, focusing on its convergence properties as the number of samples and the dimensionality of the feature space increase. We will derive a consistent estimator of the Shapley values using LeverageSHAP and examine its convergence rate under various conditions.
CONTROLS: Theoretical comparison with KernelSHAP and other existing estimators, numerical experiments to validate the theoretical results using synthetic and real-world datasets.
COST: 25,000
PREDICTION: We expect to find that LeverageSHAP converges at a faster rate than KernelSHAP, and provide a precise characterization of the convergence properties of LeverageSHAP in terms of the number of samples and the dimensionality of the feature space.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Revised KernelSHAP Analysis for High-Dimensional Data Sets
PROPOSAL: We revisit the analysis of KernelSHAP and derive non-asymptotic bounds for its sample complexity, leveraging techniques from high-dimensional statistics and randomized algorithms. This will provide a more detailed understanding of the trade-offs between the number of samples and the dimensionality of the feature space in KernelSHAP.
CONTROLS: Baseline comparison with the widely used SHAP library's implementation of KernelSHAP, ablation studies of the effect of the number of samples and the choice of kernel, as well as comparison with LeverageSHAP.
COST: 50,000
PREDICTION: We expect to find that the non-asymptotic bounds for KernelSHAP exhibit a more nuanced relationship with the dimensionality of the feature space, and provide a clearer understanding of the computational costs associated with KernelSHAP in high-dimensional settings.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Variance Reduction Techniques for Shapley Values Estimation
PROPOSAL: We apply variance reduction techniques, such as control variates and stratified sampling, to reduce the variance of Shapley values estimators like KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP. This will help improve the stability and accuracy of these estimators in high-dimensional settings.
CONTROLS: Comparison with the original KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP on several real-world datasets, as well as ablation studies to evaluate the effectiveness of each variance reduction technique.
COST: 35,000
PREDICTION: We anticipate that the variance reduction techniques will lead to significant improvements in the stability and accuracy of Shapley values estimation, particularly in high-dimensional settings where the variance of the estimators can be excessively large.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Shapley Values for Deep Neural Networks with Stratified Sampling
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel stratified sampling scheme for estimating Shapley values in deep neural networks. Our method leverages the fact that neural networks can be decomposed into layers and applies stratified sampling to reduce the variance of the Shapley values estimates.
CONTROLS: Comparison with existing methods, such as KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP, on several deep learning benchmarks, including ImageNet and CIFAR-10.
COST: 40,000
PREDICTION: We expect that our method will provide more accurate and stable Shapley values estimates, particularly for large and complex deep neural networks. This will enable more effective model-agnostic interpretability for deep learning models.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: A Theoretical Framework for Shapley Values Estimation
PROPOSAL: We develop a theoretical framework for understanding the limits of Shapley values estimation, focusing on the trade-offs between the number of samples, dimensionality, and accuracy. This framework will provide a foundation for designing more efficient and accurate Shapley values estimation methods.
CONTROLS: Theoretical analysis of existing methods, such as KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP, as well as our proposed methods.
COST: 60,000
PREDICTION: We expect that our theoretical framework will reveal fundamental limitations of Shapley values estimation and provide guidelines for designing more efficient and accurate methods. This will enable significant advancements in model-agnostic interpretability.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Scalable Shapley Values Estimation using Approximation Algorithms
PROPOSAL: We design and analyze approximation algorithms for Shapley values estimation that can scale to large datasets and high-dimensional feature spaces. Our method will leverage recent advances in approximation algorithms and machine learning to provide a scalable solution.
CONTROLS: Experimental comparison with existing methods, such as KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP, on large-scale benchmarks, such as ImageNet and CIFAR-100.
COST: 70,000
PREDICTION: We expect that our approximation algorithm will provide a significant speedup in Shapley values estimation while maintaining reasonable accuracy, enabling the application of Shapley values to large-scale and complex deep learning models.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Model-Agnostic Feature Engineering for Shapley Values Estimation
PROPOSAL: We develop a model-agnostic feature engineering approach to improve the accuracy and efficiency of Shapley values estimation. Our method will learn a subset of relevant features from the original feature space to reduce the dimensionality and improve the estimation quality.
CONTROLS: Experimental comparison with existing methods, such as KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP, on various benchmarks with high-dimensional feature spaces.
COST: 80,000
PREDICTION: We expect that our model-agnostic feature engineering approach will provide a significant improvement in the accuracy and efficiency of Shapley values estimation, especially in high-dimensional feature spaces. This will enable more effective model-agnostic interpretability for complex models.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: A Unified Benchmark for Shapley Values Estimation
PROPOSAL: We introduce a comprehensive benchmark for Shapley values estimation methods, providing a standardized evaluation framework for various algorithms and techniques. Our benchmark will enable fair comparison, reproducibility, and knowledge sharing in the Shapley values estimation community.
CONTROLS: Experimental comparison with existing methods, as well as our proposed methods, on a diverse range of benchmarks and datasets.
COST: 100,000
PREDICTION: We expect that our unified benchmark will become a fundamental resource for the development and evaluation of Shapley values estimation methods, accelerating progress in model-agnostic interpretability and decision support for complex models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Current Foundation Models for Temporal Understanding in Satellite Image Time Series
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) and diffusion-based image generators on three tasks: static image captioning of a single satellite image, temporal change description of a short sequence (3-5 images), and future satellite image forecasting over the same short sequence. Use a diverse set of real-world satellite image datasets, including Google Earth Engine's Landsat and Sentinel-2 data. Measure performance using a combination of metrics, including BLEU, Meteor, and the new Temporal Consistency (TC) metric (defined as the similarity between the predicted change and the actual change in the next time step).
CONTROLS: Use each model as a baseline for the three tasks, and compare the performance of different architectures and training regimes within each model family. For diffusion-based image generators, experiment with different scheduler optimization methods (e.g., Adam, SGD) and number of denoising steps. For MLLMs, compare the performance of models pre-trained on different datasets (e.g., LAION, Clip) and fine-tuned on satellite image tasks.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: The study will highlight the limitations of current foundation models in temporal understanding and change description, and identify areas for improvement. MLLMs will likely perform better in change description tasks due to their ability to reason about high-level concepts, but will struggle with long-range temporal dynamics. Diffusion-based models will show improvement with increasing denoising steps, but will still lag behind MLLMs in change description tasks. The TC metric will demonstrate its effectiveness in evaluating temporal consistency.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Addressing Long-Range Temporal Dynamics with Incremental Self-Supervised Learning
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel self-supervised learning paradigm that injects sparse and temporal coherence into the training process of foundation models, addressing the long-range temporal dynamics deficit. Incrementally add new images to the training sequence, requiring the model to continuously align with the observed changes, rather than processing the entire sequence at once. Introduce a novel Temporal Coherence Loss (TCL) that positively rewards models for preserving changes observed in previous time steps and negatively rewards models that introduce novel information before it is observed in the data. Train the model on a real-world satellite image dataset with a large, irregularly sampled sequence of images.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed incremental self-supervised learning approach to standard self-supervised learning and supervised learning methods. For ablation studies, also train the model with the TCL loss alone, without incremental learning, and with incremental learning alone (without TCL). Compare the performance of models trained with different self-supervised learning objectives (e.g., contrastive, autoencoding).
COST: 6000
PREDICTION: The approach will significantly improve the long-range temporal dynamics of foundation models, leading to improved performance in change description and forecasting tasks. The TCL loss will be shown to be essential for capturing the temporal coherence of changes in the data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Harnessing Multimodal Information for Temporal Change Description
PROPOSAL: Introduce a multimodal transformer-based architecture that fuses visual and text information to generate a natural-language description of the key dynamic changes in a satellite image time series. Train the model on a large-scale real-world satellite image dataset with paired text annotations, and evaluate its performance on the Temporal Change Description task. Explore the use of vision-and-language pre-training objectives, such as pet but also compare with other state of art mms for cross-modal fusion such as   contr им contrastive learning
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the proposed multimodal architecture to unimodal visual-only and text-only baselines, as well as state-of-the-art change description models that lack multimodal fusion. Also, evaluate the contribution of different pre-training objectives and tasks (e.g., image-text retrieval, captioning) to the performance of the multimodal model.
COST: 8000
PREDICTION: The multimodal architecture will significantly outperform unimodal baselines and previous change description models, particularly in capturing the underlying causal narrative of changes. The model will demonstrate a strong ability to reason about the relationships between visual and text information, leading to more accurate and informative change descriptions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Improving Temporal Consistency in Future Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Propose a novel module to assess and correct the temporal consistency of future satellite image forecasts generated by a diffusion-based image generator. Train a separate probabilistic model to predict the temporal probability distribution of changes in the forecasted image, and use this distribution to scale and correct the forecasted changes. Evaluate the performance of the proposed module on a real-world satellite image dataset with a long and irregularly sampled sequence of images.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the proposed module to a baseline approach that generates future images without temporal consistency corrections. Also, evaluate the contribution of different probability distribution approximation methods (e.g., Gaussian, Laplace) to the performance of the proposed module.
COST: 9000
PREDICTION: The proposed module will significantly improve the temporal consistency of future satellite image forecasts, leading to improved performance in forecasting tasks. The probabilistic model will demonstrate a strong ability to predict the temporal distribution of changes, allowing for more accurate and consistent forecasts.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Improving Temporal Consistency in Future Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Introduce a temporal coherence-aware diffusion-based image generator that directly learns to model the temporal probability distribution of changes in the forecasted image. Train the model on a real-world satellite image dataset with a long and irregularly sampled sequence of images, and evaluate its performance on future satellite image forecasting tasks. Use a novel Temporal Sequential Denoising Diffusion (TSDD) model that incorporates a probabilistic temporal coherence module to learn the temporal distribution of changes.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the TSDD model to state-of-the-art diffusion-based image generators that lack temporal coherence awareness. Also, evaluate the contribution of different temporal probability distribution approximation methods (e.g., Gaussian, Laplace) to the performance of the TSDD model.
COST: 12000
PREDICTION: The TSDD model will significantly improve the temporal consistency and accuracy of future satellite image forecasts, outperforming state-of-the-art diffusion-based image generators. The temporal coherence-aware diffusion process will allow for more accurate and robust forecasting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Land-Use Change Monitoring with Temporally-aware Object Detection
PROPOSAL: Develop a temporally-aware object detection model that can accurately detect and track changes in land use and land cover over time. Introduce a novel spatiotemporal attention mechanism that allows the model to focus on the most relevant temporal information when detecting changes. Evaluate the performance of the proposed model on a large-scale real-world satellite image dataset with annotated land use and land cover changes. Compare the performance of the proposed model to state-of-the-art object detection models that lack temporal awareness.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the proposed model to different object detection models (e.g., Faster R-CNN, Mask R-CNN) that lack temporal attention. Also, evaluate the contribution of different spatiotemporal attention mechanisms (e.g., convolutional, recurrent) to the performance of the proposed model.
COST: 11000
PREDICTION: The proposed model will significantly improve the accuracy and robustness of land use and land cover change detection, outperforming state-of-the-art object detection models. The temporally-aware object detection model will allow for more accurate tracking of changes and earlier detection of anomalies.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE: Land-Use Change Monitoring with Temporally-aware Object Detection
PROPOSAL: Introduce a multi-task learning framework that trains the temporally-aware object detection model on both object detection and land use classification tasks. Use a shared feature extractor to learn spatial and temporal features that are effective for both tasks. Evaluate the performance of the proposed model on a large-scale real-world satellite image dataset with annotated object detection and land use classification. Compare the performance of the proposed model to state-of-the-art models that train on each task separately.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the proposed model to different multi-task learning frameworks (e.g., task-sharing, task-flipping) and different feature extractors (e.g., convolutional, recurrent). Also, evaluate the contribution of different task weighting strategies to the performance of the proposed model.
COST: 14000
PREDICTION: The proposed model will significantly improve the accuracy and robustness of land use and land cover change detection, outperforming state-of-the-art models. The multi-task learning framework will allow the model to learn spatial and temporal features that are effective for both object detection and land use classification.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficiency-Consistency Tradeoff in Satellite Image Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Investigate the efficiency-consistency tradeoff in satellite image time series forecasting models. Analyze the Pareto front of forecasting models with respect to efficiency and consistency, and propose new models that can balance these conflicting objectives. Evaluate the performance of the proposed models on a range of real-world satellite image datasets with different temporal resolutions and observation frequencies. Compare the performance of the proposed models to state-of-the-art models that prioritize either efficiency or consistency.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the proposed models to different ensemble methods (e.g., bagging, boosting) and different model compression techniques (e.g., quantization, pruning). Also, evaluate the contribution of different temporal sampling strategies to the performance of the proposed models.
COST: 16000
PREDICTION: The proposed models will significantly improve the efficiency-consistency tradeoff in satellite image time series forecasting, allowing for faster computation while maintaining accurate and consistent forecasts. The analysis will reveal the optimal balance between efficiency and consistency for different applications and use cases.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Uncertainty-Aware Satellite Image Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Develop a uncertainty-aware satellite image time series forecasting model that can quantify and reason with the uncertainty of its predictions. Introduce a novel probabilistic framework that models the predictive uncertainty of the model as a function of the input data and the model's internal state. Evaluate the performance of the proposed model on a range of real-world satellite image datasets with different temporal resolutions and observation frequencies. Compare the performance of the proposed model to state-of-the-art models that lack uncertainty awareness.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the proposed model to different uncertainty quantification methods (e.g., Monte Carlo dropout, Bayesian neural networks). Also, evaluate the contribution of different probabilistic frameworks (e.g., Gaussian processes, Markov chains) to the performance of the proposed model.
COST: 18000
PREDICTION: The proposed model will significantly improve the uncertainty-awareness of satellite image time series forecasting, allowing for more reliable and accurate predictions. The probabilistic framework will enable the model to reason with the uncertainty of its predictions and provide more transparent and trustworthy forecasts.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: System Integration and Real-World Deployment of Satellite Image Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Develop a comprehensive system integration framework that combines the satellite image time series forecasting models with real-world data sources and interfaces. Provide a cloud-based platform for data ingestion, model training, and prediction serving, and evaluate the performance of the system on a large-scale real-world dataset. Compare the performance of the proposed system to state-of-the-art satellite image time series forecasting systems.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the proposed system to different cloud-based platforms (e.g., AWS, Google Cloud) and different data ingestion and serving mechanisms (e.g., Apache Kafka, Apache Flink).
COST: 20000
PREDICTION: The proposed system will significantly improve the efficiency and effectiveness of satellite image time series forecasting, enabling real-world applications and deployments. The system will demonstrate the potential for large-scale deployment and real-world impact.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Effectiveness of Frozen Ensembles for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of frozen ensembles (pre-trained models that are not updated) against their updated counterparts using online gradient descent on traffic flow forecasting datasets. Specifically, we will use the Metro and PEMS-B datasets and evaluate models using Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Mean Squared Error (MSE) metrics. We will freeze the parameters of the ensemble models and only update a small adapter module, consisting of 3 fully connected layers with 128, 64, and 32 units respectively. Controls will include baseline models that freeze all parameters, baseline models that do not freeze any parameters, and a learning rate schedule for OGD that adapts to the changing distribution. 
CONTROLS: Baseline model 1: frozen all parameters, Baseline model 2: unfrozen parameters, Baseline model 3: learning rate adaptation for OGD.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: The frozen ensemble model should consistently perform better than the baseline models when the distribution shifts, but might underperform when the changes are abrupt, as updates to the adapter module may take time to react.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Model-Based vs. Data-Driven Reweighting for Online Gradient Descent
PROPOSAL: Investigate two different reweighting strategies to reduce variance in online gradient descent for time series forecasting. First, we will use model-based reweighting: dynamically adjust the weights of the training data to reflect their importance, using a slowly updated distribution over the data. Second, we will use data-driven reweighting: directly fit a weighted least squares problem to the data, where the weights are computed based on the distances between each data point and the reference distribution. We will evaluate both methods on electricity consumption forecasting datasets, such as the M4 Competition dataset, and compare their performance to a baseline that uses standard OGD. Controls will include ablation studies to assess the importance of the slowly updated distribution in model-based reweighting.
CONTROLS: Baseline: OGD, Baseline with slowly updated distribution: OGD with model-based reweighting but no data-driven reweighting, Baseline with equal weights: OGD with data-driven reweighting but using equal weights for all samples.
COST: 2400

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Model-Based vs. Data-Driven Reweighting for Online Gradient Descent
PROPOSAL: Make changes to the original proposal to better suit its purpose. Instead of using a slowly updated distribution from scratch, use the posterior distribution of the parameters obtained from a small batch of past data to compute sample weights. This ensures that the weights are more informative and reduces overconfidence. We also modify the data-driven reweighting approach to use a tangent number of nearest neighbors to the reference distribution, reducing the computational complexity. The rest of the proposal remains the same.
CONTROLS: Baseline: OGD, Baseline with past data posterior weights: OGD with model-based reweighting but without the slowly updated distribution, Baseline with equal weights: OGD with data-driven reweighting but using equal weights for all samples.
COST: 2000

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Meta-Learning for Fast Adaptation to Concept Drift in Deep Time Series Forecasters
PROPOSAL: Train a meta-learner with a range of tasks that reflect different concept drift scenarios in time series forecasting. For each task, the meta-learner produces a set of learned initializations that are tailored to the specific scenario. When a new adaptation task arises due to concept drift, we use the meta-learner to obtain a set of promising initializations and apply a small number of gradient descent updates to refine the model. Evaluate the performance of this approach on solar power forecasting benchmarks, such as the NSW Solar Power dataset, and compare its speed and accuracy against online gradient descent methods that adapt directly from the initial model. Controls will include variants of the meta-learner that use different architectural components and loss functions.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Direct adaptation using OGD, Baseline with pre-trained components: Meta-learning with pre-trained components but no adaptation, Baseline with fixed initialization: OGD with fixed initialization.
COST: 4200

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Meta-Learning for Fast Adaptation to Concept Drift in Deep Time Series Forecasters
PROPOSAL: Refine the original proposal by incorporating techniques to better handle delayed and noisy feedback in multi-step time series forecasting. When adapting to concept drift, we allow the model to incorporate information from past predictions and updates, rather than solely relying on current data. Additionally, we introduce a meta-critic component that assesses the quality of the past predictions and selectively updates the model based on this feedback. Evaluate the performance of this approach on exchange rate forecasting benchmarks, such as the OANDA Exchange Rate dataset, and compare its performance to state-of-the-art methods for handling delayed and noisy feedback.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Direct adaptation using OGD with delayed and noisy feedback, Baseline with feedback aggregation: Aggregation of past predictions and updates, Baseline with fixed initialization: OGD with fixed initialization and delayed and noisy feedback.
COST: 3200

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Memory-Augmented Online Gradient Descent for Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Introduce an external memory component to the online gradient descent algorithm, allowing the model to selectively store and retrieve relevant past data points to reduce the variance of the gradient estimates. Store the embedded past data points in a graph-based memory structure, which enables efficient retrieval of relevant data points based on their similarity with the current data point. Evaluate the performance of this approach on weather forecasting datasets, such as the Num_forecast dataset, and compare its performance to existing methods that use additional memory structures. Controls will include variants of the memory module that use different node and edge representations.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard OGD, Baseline with graph-based memory: Adding graph-based memory without the online gradient descent component, Baseline with equal sampling: OGD with the same number of samples taken uniformly from the past data.
COST: 5600

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Model-Based vs. Data-Driven Reweighting for Online Gradient Descent
PROPOSAL: Revise the original proposal by incorporating an ensemble method to combine the strengths of both model-based and data-driven reweighting strategies. At each adaptation step, train a model-based reweighting component and a data-driven reweighting component in parallel, and then combine their outputs using a weighting scheme. Evaluate the performance of this ensemble approach on traffic flow forecasting datasets, such as the PEMS-B dataset, and compare its performance to the individual model-based and data-driven reweighting methods.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard OGD, Baseline with model-based reweighting: OGD with model-based reweighting but without the data-driven reweighting component, Baseline with data-driven reweighting: OGD with data-driven reweighting but without the model-based reweighting component.
COST: 3800

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Theoretical Bounds for Dynamic Regret in Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Derive theoretical bounds for the dynamic regret of online gradient descent in the context of time series forecasting. Consider a setting where the data distribution changes over time, and the goal is to minimize the cumulative loss incurred by the model. Provide a new analysis of the dynamic regret and obtain explicit bounds on its performance. Compare these bounds to existing theoretical results for online optimization. This proposal will provide a theoretical foundation for understanding the performance of online gradient descent in time series forecasting tasks.

COST: 4800

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Distributionally Robust Approach to Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Introduce a distributionally robust approach to online time series forecasting that involves minimizing a worst-case expected loss over a set of potential distributions. This approach would be less sensitive to the specific changes in the data distribution than traditional online gradient descent methods. Evaluate the performance of this approach on electricity transformer temperature forecasting datasets and compare its performance to existing methods that use robust optimization.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard OGD, Baseline with robust optimization: Using robust optimization but without the online gradient descent component, Baseline with fixed uncertainty set: Using a fixed uncertainty set for robust optimization but without adaptation.
COST: 6200

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE: Theoretical Bounds for Dynamic Regret in Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Revise the original proposal by incorporating the results from the distributionally robust approach into the theoretical analysis. Derive a refined bound for the dynamic regret that takes into account the robust optimization approach. This bound would provide a more realistic estimate of the performance of online gradient descent methods in practice. Provide a comparison between the original bound and the refined bound to demonstrate the impact of the distributionally robust approach on the theoretical guarantees.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating BM25 as a Light Baseline for Hybrid Visual Retrieval
PROPOSAL: We will evaluate the performance of BM25, a classical sparse lexical model, on the MS-COCO Captions and Visual Genome datasets as a primary retriever, and compare its results with ColPali-based encoders. We will use the same late-interaction framework as ColPali to train and evaluate BM25 on these benchmarks.
CONTROLS: BM25 alone, ColPali-based encoders alone
COST: 18000
PREDICTION: BM25 will show a large performance gap compared to ColPali-based encoders, but will still provide a reasonable baseline to compare against. However, its performance may fail on details such as sub-figure level retrieval.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: VarEnc: A Variance-Based Aggregation Method for Hybrid Retrieval
PROPOSAL: We propose VarEnc, a lightweight aggregation method that combines the query-document representations of two heterogeneous retrievers by taking their element-wise variances into account. VarEnc works by computing the weights for each element in the representations based on their variances, which allows for robust and efficient combination of the two signals.
CONTROLS: Standard hybrid retrieval methods (e.g., weighted sum), VarEnc without heterogeneity (single-vector representations)
COST: 252000
PREDICTION: VarEnc will significantly improve the retrieval quality by exploiting the rich interactions within the representation spaces of the two retrievers, while being more efficient and practical than existing methods. However, its performance might depend heavily on the variance of the signals, and may fail on cases with very high variance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scalarization of Multi-Vector Representations for Hybrid Retrieval
PROPOSAL: We propose to use a scalarization function to transform the multi-vector representations of the two retrievers into single-vector representations that can be combined efficiently at query time. We will experiment with various scalarization functions, such as the dot product, cosine similarity, and mean, to determine the most effective approach.
CONTROLS: VarEnc, scalarized representations without VarEnc, ColPali-based encoders with single-vector representations
COST: 378000
PREDICTION: The scalarization approach will allow for efficient combination of the two signals, but may lose some of the benefits of multi-vector representations. It will be particularly interesting to see how this approach compares to VarEnc in terms of retrieval quality and efficiency. However, if the scalarization function is not carefully chosen, the performance might fail in cases with very diverse vectors.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Scalarization of Multi-Vector Representations for Hybrid Retrieval
PROPOSAL: We refine the scalarization approach by incorporating a trainable weight matrix that learns to map the multi-vector representations to a single vector that captures their most relevant features. This will allow the system to adapt to different data distributions and improve the retrieval quality.
CONTROLS: Original scalarization approach, VarEnc, scalarized representations without VarEnc, ColPali-based encoders with single-vector representations
COST: 594000
PREDICTION: The refined scalarization approach will lead to significant improvements in retrieval quality by adaptively selecting the most relevant features from the multi-vector representations. However, it may require a larger training set to learn effective weight matrices, and its performance might fail if the adaptive learning is too slow or too sensitive.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Tenant Embeddings for Hybrid Visual Retrieval
PROPOSAL: We propose to learn a shared multi-tenant embedding space for the two retrievers by adding a multi-task learning objective to their individual training losses. This will allow the two models to leverage each other's strengths and adapt to each other's data distributions.
CONTROLS: Standalone training of each retriever, attention-based fusion of the two retrievers
COST: 900000
PREDICTION: Multi-tenant embeddings will lead to significant improvements in retrieval quality by enabling the two models to share learned representations and adapt to each other's patterns. However, its performance might depend on the difficulty of the tasks and the similarity of the datasets, and may fail if the two models are too dissimilar or one model is significantly stronger than the other.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Explainability and Diagnostic Tools for Hybrid Visual Retrieval
PROPOSAL: We develop and integrate a suite of explainability and diagnostic tools to analyze the decision-making process of hybrid visual retrieval systems. These tools will provide insights into how the two retrievers interact, which features are most informative, and where the system may be failing.
CONTROLS: Baseline explainability methods, ablation studies of the two retrievers
COST: 1170000
PREDICTION: The explainability and diagnostic tools will provide actionable insights into the behavior of hybrid visual retrieval systems, enabling researchers and practitioners to optimize and improve their performance. However, the development and integration of these tools may add significant computational and interpretation overhead, and may fail to provide interpretable results if the system is too complex or the data is too noisy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: FusionNet: A Lightweight Fusion Architecture for Hybrid Visual Retrieval
PROPOSAL: We propose FusionNet, a lightweight fusion architecture that combines the strengths of the two retrievers using a hierarchical architecture with multiple fusion stages. FusionNet will adaptively focus on the most informative features from the two retrievers and learn to combine them efficiently.
CONTROLS: FusionNet with different fusion stages, standalone training of each retriever, attention-based fusion of the two retrievers
COST: 1620000
PREDICTION: FusionNet will provide state-of-the-art performance in hybrid visual retrieval by adaptively combining the strengths of the two retrievers and learning to prioritize the most informative features. However, its performance might depend on the difficulty of the tasks and the similarity of the datasets, and may fail if the two models are too dissimilar or one model is significantly stronger than the other.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transferability of Hybrid Visual Retrieval Models to Real-World Datasets
PROPOSAL: We evaluate the transferability of hybrid visual retrieval models to real-world datasets, including PubMed, arXiv, and other academic paper repositories. We will investigate the generalizability of our models to different domains and data distributions, and explore methods to improve their robustness and adaptability.
CONTROLS: FusionNet, scalarization methods, multi-tenant embeddings on PubMed and arXiv
